experiments.scope: The search of proof.md Section 4 on the exact sha3-256-r18-prefix-v1 hash, run end to end at width 22. the step generator embedded in experiments/compact.py regenerates the claimed straight line of Section 3 from the generator's decisions (embedded plan; the packed 35-bit encoding must hash to the SHA-256 printed in Section 3.6, else the program stops), checks it against a plain 18-round implementation (two chained steps of 256 points), and executes it on Python integers: one integer holds a plane for all trials of the request (trial t in bits 256 t to 256 t + 255), trials never interact. Points are 22-bit values u (upper bits zero), the message is m(u) of Section 2 (128 bytes), and after every step the planes 22 to 255 are set to zero (with the labels of the starts below, the only difference from the full-size program). Per trial: 256 walks from starts rho + i (rho from SHAKE-256 of the trial seed; the full-size program labels trail i as t(i), Section 4), distinguished point = the 4 low image bits zero and the 3 bits above them, as a number, less than 5, no trail cut, at most 3,000 trails and 400 steps per attempt, a table end -> trail number, restarts, and the replay of Section 4 (the stored trail measured by walking it to its distinguished point; trails of more than 256 evaluations refused) with the plain implementation. It returns two different messages whose 18-round digests agree on the 22 low bits.
experiments.hypothesis: Every trial returns two different messages m(a), m(b) whose digests agree on the 22 masked bits (bytes 0 and 1 and the low 6 bits of byte 2), found by walks, the table and the replay. Observations (untrusted): steps of the successful attempt, trails, attempts, table size, replayed evaluations. Our ideal-function control with the same parameters needs 20.47 steps on average (20,000 trials, sd 7.91). Nothing about the cost at 256 bits is inferred from the run.

experiments.scope: The same regenerated straight line at full width: per trial 256 uniform 256-bit points (SHAKE-256 of the trial seed), eight chained steps of the full program (2,048 evaluations per trial), and the first pair, in step-major order, of distinct evaluated inputs whose images agree on the 22 low bits; the two inputs are recomputed with the plain implementation and returned as messages m(a), m(b). A trial without such a pair returns two nulls. A success is a 22-bit partial match, not a collision.
experiments.hypothesis: If the images of the 2,048 distinct evaluated inputs are uniform on 22 bits, a trial succeeds with probability 1 - prod_(i<2048)(1 - i/2^22) = 0.3934: about 100.7 of 256 successes, standard deviation 7.8. A wrong straight line would give digests that the organizer's recomputation does not match, and failed pairs.

experiments.scope: Run the normative emitter and require the claimed instruction count, byte length and SHA-256; decode and execute that exact controller through setup, evalF, table boundaries and probe, restart and cap refusal, gather/setwalk, replay success and recovered messages, and replay failure; then return the first 12-bit projected match among 68 full-width target evaluations per trial.
experiments.hypothesis: The emitted controller bytes implement the claimed compact search paths and agree with the selected-round target function. Under uniform 12-bit projected images, 68 images repeat with probability about 0.428; the organizer recomputes returned pairs and retains null trials.

experiments.scope: Recompute the covered first-coincidence sum and every early-halt subtraction at 100-digit precision, verify each outward-rounded interval and the frozen-plan SHA-256, require the union lower endpoint to be at least 0.39, then return the same independently recomputable 12-bit target projection.
experiments.hypothesis: The live-plan random-function certificate is arithmetically self-consistent and its outward-rounded lower endpoint reaches 0.39. The returned projected pairs are target consistency checks, not inputs to the certificate.
